sources.cite: Myers V. When something goes wrong: how to disclose an error. American Nurse Journal, 2011-10-11
sources.note: Relayed from the NCLEX-RN case insulin-given-to-wrong-bed, not re-read for this band; its note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch with quotes: 'Noting mistakes and reporting them is the responsibility of all healthcare providers'; 'Trigger your chain of command if there is an event', with the author notifying her head nurse and the physician immediately after her own medication error; 'Disclosure is required per professional, legal and regulatory standards', usually led by the physician, nursing leadership or a team and planned; questions answered as honestly as possible.

sources.cite: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee. 6. Glycemic Goals, Hypoglycemia, and Hyperglycemic Crises: Standards of Care in Diabetes-2026. Diabetes Care 2026;49(Suppl 1):S132-S149
sources.note: Relayed from the NCLEX-RN case insulin-given-to-wrong-bed, not re-read for this band; its note: Relayed from the LPN/VN case ltc-insulin-hypoglycemia (read 2026-11-11, primary text), not re-read: level 1 hypoglycemia is glucose under 70 and at least 54 mg/dL, level 2 under 54; glucose is preferred for the conscious person under 70, repeated if still low 15 minutes later.
